subject: Convergence MAP — security acceptance criteria, DPA carveouts & archival SLAs
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acornbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acorn Bank Legal <legal@acornbank.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — SOC 2 & DPA clarifications

Marcus — thanks for the MAP you shared yesterday. A few legal/security items popped up when we reviewed with procurement and legal: 

1) DPA carveouts: we need confirmation of whether Redwood will accept a contract annex for EU data residency exceptions (some wallets will route EU PII out of region). If not, we need a proposal for an escrow/archival option.

2) SOC 2 evidence: our auditors want a list of artifacts and an estimated delivery date for the items you can provide (test reports, control descriptions, penetration test summary). Can you confirm which items are in scope for hosted vs private deployments?

3) CAIQ/SIG: our security team prefers a completed CAIQ; a partially completed matrix won’t pass their gating. Is there an ETA for the CAIQ completion?

We’re trying to keep the MAP timeline tight (goal: decision on purchase by 2026-09-30). Can you propose specific acceptance criteria and dates we can commit to in the MAP?

Thanks — Emily
Emily Zhang
Senior Procurement Manager
Acorn Bank

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acornbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — SOC 2 & DPA clarifications

Emily — appreciate the clear list. Quick summary and proposal below so we can slot this into the MAP (I attached a DPA carveouts draft and a CAIQ workplan):

DPA carveouts / residency
- Redwood hosted: default is multi-region with optional region pinning for Dedicated/Private. For EU-residency needs we propose: 1) region pinning (Dedicated or Private), or 2) archival escrow via customer-controlled S3 (encrypted) for hosted customers with EU residency constraints.
- Proposal: we will accept an Acorn-specific annex that limits cross-border processing for PII fields you flag. Attached: redwood-dpa-carveouts-v1.pdf (draft annex).

SOC 2 evidence scope & ETA
- What we can provide immediately: SOC 2 Type II summary report, control narrative index, penetration test summary (redacted), and an evidence index (soc2-evidence-index.csv).
- Hosted vs Private: hosted items above apply to hosted API customers; Private deployments get the same artifacts plus deployment-specific runbooks (delivery timeline depends on provisioning).
- ETA: initial evidence bundle available by 2026-09-13; full control-package (for auditors) by 2026-09-20 (we will mark items that require an NDA or additional carveouts).

CAIQ/SIG
- Current status: CAIQ baseline completed — we are finishing detailed answers for the last 12 items (data residency, key management edge cases, and archival).
- ETA for completed CAIQ: 2026-09-15. Draft attached: caiaq-response-draft.md.

Recommended MAP acceptance criteria (suggested milestones)
- M1 (by 2026-09-13): Initial evidence bundle delivered + DPA annex draft agreed in principle.
- M2 (by 2026-09-20): Completed SOC 2 control package and CAIQ submitted to Acorn security.
- M3 (by 2026-09-27): Final redlines agreed (legal) and DocuSign envelope prepared.
- M4 (by 2026-09-30): Contract executed and onboarding kickoff scheduled.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you confirm the SOC 2 items and the exact filenames we’ll hand over on 9/13 and 9/20? Soojin — can you confirm the archival/escrow feasibility notes below?

Marcus Lin
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-dpa-carveouts-v1.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acornbank.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — SOC 2 & DPA clarifications

Emily / Marcus — quick confirmation on artifacts we’ll deliver: 

Deliverables on 2026-09-13 (initial bundle)
- SOC2_TypeII_summary_202605.pdf (summary report, redacted client names)
- control-narrative-index.csv (list of controls with owner/contact)
- pen-test-summary-202605.pdf (executive summary, scope & remediation status)
- soc2-evidence-index.csv (mapping of controls to available artifacts; items requiring NDA flagged)

Deliverables on 2026-09-20 (full control-package)
- control-evidence-archive.zip (links and instructions to access evidence via secure portal)
- runbook-hosted-deployment.pdf (operational controls for hosted)
- runbook-private-deployment.pdf (deployment-specific docs for Private)

Notes:
- A handful of evidence items include third-party vendor logs (retention 90 days) — if Acorn needs raw logs extended we’ll need a scoped addendum.
- We will redact any customer-identifying data before delivery.

Happy to walk through the bundle in a 30-min review call once you’ve had a chance to scan.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acornbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — SOC 2 & DPA clarifications

Emily — technical clarifications on archival / escrow options and key management: 

1) Archival escrow (hosted customers)
- Mechanism: nightly encrypted snapshots (AES-256) written to a customer-designated S3 bucket in the region you pick (we will provide object lifecycle rules you can adopt). Snapshots contain only message metadata and audit logs for the evaluation period, not full PII by default unless unredacted export is requested.
- Access: customer-managed KMS keys supported (you control key rotation). Redwood will provide a read-only role for legal/audit retrieval when a documented escrow process is triggered.

2) Key management & CAIQ notes
- For dedicated/private: customer KMS/HSM integrations are supported (we use industry-standard KMIP or cloud-native KMS APIs).
- CAIQ items flagged: eKey custody for archived exports (we will confirm exact QIDs on 9/15).

3) Retention windows
- Default: ephemeral request logs 30 days; aggregated telemetry 90 days; account artifacts retained per contract (default 365 days).
- If Acorn needs a longer retention for audit purposes, propose a 3rd-party-hosted archival lane (retention to be defined in annex).

I can add these details to the CAIQ responses and the DPA annex draft.

Soojin Lee
Security Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acornbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Acorn Bank Legal <legal@acornbank.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — SOC 2 & DPA clarifications

Marcus / Kimberly / Soojin — thank you, this is helpful and much clearer. Two quick items before we lock the MAP: 

- Legal wants the DPA annex populated with a list of the exact PII fields we expect to be covered by the residency carveout. I’ll send a redline by EOD tomorrow.
- For retention, Acorn will request the 365-day artifact retention but asks for evidence that archived exports (escrow) can be delivered within 48 hours once triggered. Can you confirm SLA on export readiness?

If you can confirm export SLA and accept the redline approach for the annex we’ll include M1–M4 in the MAP and aim to sign by 9/30. I’ll schedule the 30-min evidence review for 9/14 in the meantime.

Best — Emily
Emily Zhang
Senior Procurement Manager
Acorn Bank
